title: X Feed Digest
summary: AI chatter in this batch was much more about operating models than model launches: scheduled jobs, parallel agent sessions, and verified-feedback loops were the real workflow upgrades people kept circling.
The strongest macro signal was geopolitical rather than earnings-driven: Hormuz blockade rhetoric and Iran-deal uncertainty remain obvious watchpoints for oil, shipping, and broader risk sentiment.

On valuation, the cleanest markets datapoint was that both forward and trailing S&P 500 P/E ratios are still above their 5-year and 10-year averages, so the tape remains expensive even if sentiment feels calmer.

Several of the most useful business threads were really about trust moats: Sam’s Club China framed as a food-safety brand, hospital consolidation as a policy-driven cost problem, and passkeys finally becoming practical enough for mainstream users.

items.title: @tychozzz: Codex Scheduled Market Briefs
items.body: A practical workflow tip: use Codex scheduled tasks to generate a daily U.S. market briefing automatically, with the prompt tuned to your own investing style. The interesting part is not the template itself but the shift toward lightweight recurring agent jobs replacing more manual research routines.

items.title: @bcherny: Claude Code Auto Mode
items.body: Bcherny’s advice was to lean on auto mode so long-running coding sessions can proceed without constant permission interrupts. The payoff is operational: you can let one session work while you move to another, which is a better pattern for serious multi-tasking with agents.

items.title: @MaxForAI: Verified-Feedback Proof Agents
items.body: A standout technical thread described DeepMind’s AlphaProof Nexus setup: models draft Lean proofs, a verifier rejects bad attempts, and multi-agent search keeps iterating until the proof is mechanically valid. It’s a strong example of where agent systems get more reliable once success is externally checkable instead of purely judged by the model.

items.title: @MaxForAI: Resume-Driven Open Source PR Spam
items.body: Another useful warning: some training programs are reportedly teaching students to submit low-value PRs to major open-source projects just to decorate résumés. The real takeaway is that OSS maintainers are absorbing more screening cost, which makes genuine newcomer contributions harder too.

items.title: @grok: Better Image-to-Video Lip Sync
items.body: xAI says Grok Imagine now has noticeably better lip sync and sharper audio for image-to-video generations. If it holds up in practice, the bigger signal is that consumer video tools are converging on polish problems like dialogue alignment rather than just raw generation novelty.

items.title: @WatcherGuru: Hormuz Blockade Still in Play
items.body: Trump said the Strait of Hormuz blockade would remain in force until an agreement with Iran is signed. Whether or not the posture changes quickly, it keeps oil, tanker traffic, and geopolitical risk pricing squarely on the watchlist.

items.title: @FactSet: S&P Valuations Stay Rich
items.body: FactSet posted that both the forward 12-month and trailing 12-month P/E ratios for the S&P 500 remain above their 5-year and 10-year averages. That is a clean reminder that U.S. equities are still trading at a premium even after a lot of macro noise has normalized.

items.title: @Dune: Kalshi + Polymarket in One Schema
items.body: Dune launched a unified Kalshi and Polymarket dataset with hourly candles and per-fill trade data. For macro or event-driven researchers, the practical value is easier comparison and backtesting across the two prediction venues without hand-rolling multiple pipelines.

items.title: @lidangzzz: Sam’s China as a Trust Moat
items.body: A sharp consumer-business thesis argued Sam’s Club China should stop imitating bulk wholesale formats and lean harder into a Whole Foods-like premium grocery model built on supply-chain control and food-safety trust. The deeper point is that in anxious consumer markets, trust can become the product as much as the groceries themselves.

items.title: @lidangzzz: Pig-Kidney Transplant Clears 200 Days
items.body: A Chinese post highlighted a Xijing Hospital xenotransplant case in which a pig-kidney recipient reportedly passed 200 postoperative days. If that durability continues, it is one of the clearest signs in the batch that organ-supply science is inching toward something operational rather than purely experimental.

items.title: @HospitalWatchUS: Hospital Consolidation Costs
items.body: A policy thread pointed to research arguing that federal rules are helping large hospital systems consolidate, weaken competition, and raise costs. The useful framing is that healthcare inflation is not just a clinical problem; it is also a structure-and-incentives problem.

items.title: @lifehacker: Passkeys Finally Feel Viable
items.body: Lifehacker’s take was that passkeys were already better than passwords, but an Apple-side change was needed before they felt practical enough to use broadly. That makes this less a cryptography story than a product-UX one: security tools only win once the friction drops.

items.title: @TheEconomist: Electrolyte Hype Check
items.body: The Economist pushed back on the flood of electrolyte-supplement marketing and suggested most claims deserve skepticism. It is a nice reminder that wellness products often sell optimization first and actual necessity second.
